subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<name>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill directory, or remain a prompt/eligibility toggle with hard isolation handled by a separate policy?
rationale: The requested fix changes the public meaning of an existing UI/config toggle and crosses security, compatibility, sandbox, and tool-execution ownership boundaries.

options.title: Make disabled hard-deny
options.body: Treat `enabled: false` as both prompt eligibility and a hard filesystem/exec boundary, with upgrade notes and central enforcement.

options.title: Add strict isolation separately
options.body: Keep the current compatibility semantics and introduce an explicit strict skill-isolation policy/UI state for hard denial.

options.title: Document trusted-code semantics
options.body: Keep disabled skills as prompt-hidden only and update UI/docs so operators use sandbox and tool policy for isolation.

recommendation.title: Make disabled hard-deny
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled: false` as both prompt eligibility and a hard filesystem/exec boundary, with upgrade notes and central enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-tool, security-doc, and agent-runtime history makes this the best available routing owner for the security boundary decision.
